one_liner: NHTSA analyst helping States improve crash, driver, vehicle, and EMS data systems through assessments, grants review, working groups, and data standards.
fit_summary: The specialized experience is narrow: you must have a year at GS-11 level authoring or leading traffic records/highway safety data programs and defining data quality metrics. Daniel's IEM consulting and intergovernmental relationship skills help with the coordination piece, but nothing on file shows traffic records or highway safety data work, so qualifying is unlikely unless Daniel's IEM projects actually touched these systems.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) as well as federal employees; you do not need status.

GS-12 requires one year of GS-11-equivalent experience covering all three elements: leading traffic records/safety data programs, analyzing data elements and defining accuracy/timeliness/completeness metrics, and coordinating federal-State-local working groups.
GS-13 requires GS-12-equivalent experience setting data standards or auditing highway safety data, and leading cross-jurisdictional upgrade initiatives.
Background investigation, Selective Service registration if applicable, and a one-year probationary period are required.
All qualifications must be met by the 10/30/2026 closing date.
keywords: crash, citation/adjudication, driver licensing, vehicle registration
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether any IEM work involved transportation, crash, EMS, or other state data systems; if not, you likely cannot truthfully meet all three GS-12 elements and should prioritize other postings.

If you do have relevant work, apply at GS-12 only. Write each two-page resume entry with your title, MM/YYYY dates, and hours per week, and describe the data program work in the posting's exact language.

Answer the narrative questions in full paragraphs that begin with the exact title, organization, dates, full/part-time status, and hours, matching your resume, because unsupported claims will be disallowed.

Use your preparedness and recovery consulting to show federal-State-local coordination, working group facilitation, briefings to senior officials, and grant or plan review, but only where it is accurate.
Preview the questionnaire on USAJOBS, rate yourself honestly, and submit before 11:59 PM Eastern on 10/30/2026; the window is only two weeks.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [number] working sessions with [federal/State/local] officials to [improve/implement] [data system or program] for [client], producing [deliverable].
Analyzed [dataset/system] data elements and defined [metric, e.g., completeness rate] to measure [accuracy/timeliness], resulting in [outcome].
Briefed [senior executives/State administrators] on [topic] and drafted [plan/guidance/policy] adopted by [client/agency].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a working group of State and local officials to improve a data system. What was your role and the outcome?
How would you define and measure timeliness, accuracy, and completeness for a State crash data system?
Walk us through how you would review a State traffic records strategic plan or a safety data improvement grant application.
Tell us about a high-level briefing you delivered to senior leaders and how you tailored it.
watch_outs: The specialized experience is very domain-specific (traffic records, MMUCC, STRAP, TRIPRS), and general emergency management consulting likely won't qualify.
HR reviews only two pages of your resume and cross-checks every claim, so any narrative detail not on the resume will be disallowed.
Applications close 10/30/2026 after a two-week window.
The position requires travel with a government travel card, and the job is in DC with telework but not remote, which means a commute from Manassas.
